mainTopic: How the words of the נזיר פסוק teach when a נזיר (and others) may become impure to bury a מת מצוה, according to the first ברייתא and רבי עקיבא.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about whether a נזיר may become impure to bury a מת מצוה, a dead person with no one else to bury him. The words 'לאביו ולאמו' seem to teach that he may. The ברייתא checks whether logic could teach this instead, but comparing the נזיר to a כהן גדול or to a כהן הדיוט points in opposite directions. When the פסוק is challenged as needed for its plain meaning, the ברייתא splits up the relatives. 'לאביו' gives the ban, 'לאחיו' allows a מת מצוה, and 'ולאמו' is used for רבי's גזירה שוה. 'לאחותו' teaches that even someone on his way to bring his פסח or circumcise his son must stop for a מת מצוה, though not for a relative. רבי עקיבא then reads the פסוקים differently: 'נפשות' and 'מת' give the ban, and 'לאחיו' covers someone who is both a כהן גדול and a נזיר. The גמרא shows how רבי עקיבא gets רבי's rule, and how רבי ישמעאל knows the case of a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר. It ends by explaining that 'אחותו' teaches that a מת מצוה overrides even מצוות punished with כרת.

steps.title: The words 'for his father and mother' allow impurity for a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the phrase 'לאביו ולאמו' teaches that a נזיר may not become impure for his parents, but he may become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the verse teach with 'for his father and for his mother'? It is for his father and mother that he may not become impure, but he may become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its reading of the פסוק: the words 'לאביו ולאמו' limit the ban on טומאה, so a נזיר may still become impure to bury a מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the phrase as setting a limit. He may not become impure for his own parents, and that is the only kind of burial excluded. Burying a מת מצוה, a dead person with no one else to bury him, stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. A phrase that introduces a lesson drawn from a פסוק.
An unattended corpse with no one else to bury it. Burying it is a special obligation.
Becomes ritually impure (here, through contact with the dead).

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying
'For his father and for his mother'?
It is for his father and for his mother that he may not become impure,
but he may become impure for a met מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes a derivation that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר may not become impure for his parents, but he may become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.title: Could logic teach this without the verse, by comparing to a כהן גדול?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests the rule could be learned by logic. A כהן גדול may not become impure for his father but may for a מת מצוה, so a נזיר should be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even without the verse, I could learn it by logic. General bans on impurity are stated for a כהן גדול and for a נזיר. Just as a כהן גדול may not become impure for his father but may for a מת מצוה, so too a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether the derivation from the פסוק is even needed. It suggests that comparing a נזיר to a כהן גדול would give the same answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a כהן גדול and a נזיר have general bans against becoming impure from the dead. For a כהן גדול we already know he may not become impure for his father but may for a מת מצוה. If the נזיר follows that model, the phrase 'לאביו ולאמו' would not be needed for this lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: I could learn it by logical reasoning.
General statements (here, the general bans on becoming impure from the dead).
The High Priest.
A person who has taken a vow of נזירות.

phrases.english: Even before it was stated,
phrases.notes: Literally 'before it is said.' He means: even if the פסוק had not said this.

phrases.english: I have a way to derive it by logic:
General prohibitions were stated about a High Priest,
and general prohibitions were stated about a nazirite.
Just as with the general prohibitions stated about a High Priest,
he may not become impure for his father,
but he may become impure for a met מצוה,
so too with the general prohibitions stated about a nazirite,
he may not become impure for his father,
but he may become impure for a met מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יֵאָמֵר יֵשׁ לִי בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the verse-based derivation in step 1 is necessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to derive the מת מצוה permission from 'לאביו ולאמו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A logical comparison to a כהן גדול would already give the same rule, so the verse seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Maybe the נזיר should be compared to a regular כהן instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the logical comparison. One could just as well compare a נזיר to a כהן הדיוט, who may become impure for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: general bans are stated for a regular כהן and for a נזיר. Just as a regular כהן may become impure for his father, so too a נזיר may become impure for his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that the logic from step 2 doesn't hold up, because a different comparison is just as reasonable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן הדיוט also has general bans on becoming impure from the dead, yet he may become impure for his father. If the נזיר were modeled on him, a נזיר could also become impure for his father. Since logic could point either way, it cannot decide the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Go this way instead. Introduces an equally strong opposite comparison.
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול.

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not saying a נזיר really may become impure for his father. It only shows that logic alone could lead there, so we need the פסוק.

phrases.english: Or perhaps go this way:
General prohibitions were stated about a common priest,
and general prohibitions were stated about a nazirite.
Just as with the general prohibitions stated about a common priest,
he may become impure for his father,
so too with the general prohibitions stated about a nazirite,
he may become impure for his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical comparison proposed in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logical comparison to a כהן גדול.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An equally valid comparison to a כהן הדיוט gives the opposite result, so the logic cannot decide.

steps.title: So the verse is needed after all
steps.stepSummary: Since logic cannot decide, the ברייתא returns to the פסוק: 'לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא' implies that a נזיר may become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: 'For his father and for his mother he shall not become impure.' This implies that he may become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: Having knocked down the logical route, the ברייתא goes back to the פסוק as the real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two comparisons cancel each other out, the פסוק is needed. The ברייתא again reads its words as a limit: only parents are excluded, so a מת מצוה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not become impure.
This implies. Introduces what we learn by inference from the words.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states:
'For his father or for his mother he shall not become impure,'
which implies that he may become impure for a met מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 rejects the logic, this returns to the verse derivation from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logic fails, so the verse is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule could have been learned by comparing a נזיר to a כהן גדול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Logic is inconclusive, so the פסוק 'לאביו ולאמו' is the source for permitting a מת מצוה.

steps.title: But the verse is needed to forbid impurity for his father
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges the derivation. The phrase 'לאביו ולאמו' seems needed for its plain meaning: a נזיר may not become impure for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is needed to teach that he may not become impure for his father!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא attacks the derivation in step 4. It sets up the next move, which will have to explain how the verse can teach both lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 showed that logic might allow a נזיר to become impure for his father, as a כהן הדיוט does. So the פסוק is needed just to forbid that. If the verse is used for its basic meaning, how can it also teach the מת מצוה permission?

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for something else. A common challenge saying a verse is already used for another lesson.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic pattern. A verse used for an extra lesson must be shown to be 'free' of its basic job. The coming answer will have to find an extra word or reading.

phrases.english: But this verse is needed
to say that he may not become impure for his father?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the verse derivation that step 4 returned to.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא' to permit impurity for a מת מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is needed for its plain meaning, forbidding impurity for a father, since logic (step 3) might otherwise have allowed it. So it is not free to teach the מת מצוה rule.

steps.title: Each relative in the verse teaches something different
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers the challenge by splitting up the words. 'לאביו' gives the basic ban, 'לאחיו' shows the מת מצוה is allowed, and 'ולאמו' is used for רבי's גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'for his father' teaches that he may not become impure for his father. 'For his brother' means he may not become impure for his brother, but he may become impure for a מת מצוה. 'And for his mother' is used for a גזירה שוה, following רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 5. It gives 'לאביו' its plain meaning and moves the מת מצוה lesson over to the word 'לאחיו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the problem was that 'לאביו' could not teach two things. Now each word gets its own job. 'לאביו' gives the ban, and 'לאחיו' gives the מת מצוה allowance by implication: only for his brother is he not allowed. 'ולאמו' is used for a separate lesson, a גזירה שוה of רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the ברייתא is switching to a new explanation
A dead person with no one else to bury him; even a נזיר or כהן must bury him
A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places in the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: 'לאביו' = the ban. 'לאחיו' = he may become impure for a מת מצוה. 'ולאמו' = a גזירה שוה of רבי.

phrases.english: Rather: 'for his father' —
is to say that he may not become impure for his father.
'For his brother' he may not become impure —
phrases.notes: So the lesson about a מת מצוה, which step 5 said could not come from 'לאביו', comes from this word.

phrases.english: but for a מת מצוה he does become impure.
'And for his mother' — is for a גזירה שוה, following רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the step 5 challenge by giving 'לאביו' its plain meaning and moving the מת מצוה lesson to 'לאחיו'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives each word of the פסוק a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לאביו' seemed to have to teach both the basic ban and the מת מצוה allowance.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לאביו' teaches the ban, 'לאחיו' teaches the מת מצוה allowance, and 'ולאמו' is used for רבי's גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Why does the verse also say 'his sister'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'ולאחותו' is used for another ברייתא, which begins by asking why the word is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for his sister' is used for what was taught in a ברייתא. As it was taught: 'For his sister'. Why does the verse say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now deals with the last relative in the פסוק, the sister. It quotes another ברייתא that asks why this word is needed, and this sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban and the מת מצוה allowance were already learned from 'לאביו' and 'לאחיו'. So 'ולאחותו' looks extra. The quoted ברייתא asks what new lesson it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
Why does the verse need to say this?
His sister

phrases.english: 'And for his sister' is for what was taught in a ברייתא.
As it was taught: 'For his sister' — why does the verse say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of relatives by giving the last word, 'ולאחותו', a job, and opens a quoted ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new lesson the word 'לאחותו' teaches, since the basic rules are already known

steps.title: On the way to a big מצוה, he still may not become impure for a relative
steps.stepSummary: The quoted ברייתא describes a person going to bring his קרבן פסח or circumcise his son who hears a relative died. He may not become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose someone went to slaughter his קרבן פסח or to circumcise his son, and he heard that a relative of his died. You might think he should become impure. You say: 'He shall not become impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted ברייתא starts its answer by setting up a case: a man on his way to do an important מצוה hears that a relative died. The ruling is that he may not become impure for the relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think burying a close relative comes before the מצוה. The ברייתא says no: he stays pure and does the מצוה. This sets up the next step, which asks about a מת מצוה in the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח, the offering brought on ערב פסח
To circumcise (ברית מילה)
You might have thought

steps.confusionAlert: This case is about an ordinary person on the way to a מצוה, not about a נזיר. The ברייתא learns it from the words of the נזיר פסוק.

phrases.english: Suppose someone went to slaughter his קרבן פסח
or to circumcise his son,
and he heard that a relative of his died —
you might think he should become impure?
You say: 'He shall not become impure.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָלַךְ לִשְׁחוֹט אֶת פִּסְחוֹ וְלָמוּל אֶת בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question 'מה תלמוד לומר' by setting up the case the word 'לאחותו' is about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Someone on his way to bring his פסח or do a מילה may not become impure for a relative.

steps.title: Even then, he does become impure for a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: One might think that in this case he may not become impure even for a מת מצוה. 'לאחותו' teaches that only for his sister is he not allowed, but for a מת מצוה he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he may not become impure even for a מת מצוה. So the verse says 'for his sister': for his sister he does not become impure, but for a מת מצוה he does become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its answer. Even a person on his way to bring his פסח or do a מילה must stop and bury a מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that the מצוה comes before a relative's burial. One might then think the מצוה also comes before a מת מצוה. The word 'לאחותו' limits the ban to relatives, so a מת מצוה comes before even these important מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes impure (by dealing with a dead body)
But (this implies that)

steps.whatToRemember: A מת מצוה comes first, even before bringing the פסח or doing a ברית מילה. A close relative does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the explanation of all the relatives in the פסוק. Each word teaches its own lesson, so no word is extra.

phrases.english: You might think he may not become impure even for a מת מצוה,
so the verse says: 'For his sister' —
it is for his sister that he may not become impure,
but for a מת מצוה, he does become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יִטַּמֵּא לְמֵת מִצְוָה, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לְאַחוֹתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 8: the ban covers relatives but not a מת מצוה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'לאחותו' teaches that even someone on his way to bring the פסח or do a מילה must become impure to bury a מת מצוה, though not for a relative.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's reading: distant people, close relatives, and the מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads 'נפשות' as distant people and 'מת' as close relatives. That leaves 'לאביו ולאמו' free to teach that a נזיר may become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'Souls' means distant people. 'Dead' means close relatives. 'For his father and his mother' he may not become impure, but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different way of reading the פסוקים, from רבי עקיבא. In his reading, the basic ban on becoming impure already comes from the words 'נפשות' and 'מת'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier reading, 'לאביו' was needed for the basic ban. For רבי עקיבא, the word 'מת' already covers close relatives like a father. So the whole phrase 'לאביו ולאמו' is free, and it teaches the exception: a מת מצוה is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Distant people, meaning people who are not relatives
Close relatives
A dead person with no one else to bury him, whom anyone must bury
Becomes ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two readings. In the earlier ברייתא, 'לאביו' gave the basic ban. For רבי עקיבא the ban already comes from 'מת', so 'לאביו ולאמו' teaches only the מת מצוה exception.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"Souls" — these are the distant people,
phrases.notes: These words come from the פסוק that forbids him to come near the dead. רבי עקיבא gives each word its own job.

phrases.english: "Dead" — these are the close relatives,
"for his father and for his mother" he does not become impure,
but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first ברייתא's reading of the words, this brings רבי עקיבא's different reading of the same פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'נפשות' covers distant people and 'מת' covers relatives. 'לאביו ולאמו' teaches that a נזיר may become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.title: For his brother: even a נזיר who is also a כהן גדול may bury a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: In רבי עקיבא's reading, 'לאחיו' teaches that even someone who is both a כהן גדול and a נזיר may become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For his brother' teaches that even if he was a כהן גדול and also a נזיר, he may not become impure for his brother, but he may become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the word 'לאחיו' its own job. It covers the strictest case: a person who is a כהן גדול and a נזיר at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is both a כהן גדול and a נזיר has two sets of strict impurity laws. You might think that double strictness forbids even a מת מצוה. 'לאחיו' teaches that even he must bury a מת מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest, who may not become impure even for close relatives
A person who took a vow of נזירות and may not become impure from the dead
For his brother

steps.whyThisMatters: This exact teaching becomes the key to the answer in step 14.

phrases.english: "For his brother" —

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם הָיָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְהוּא נָזִיר,
phrases.english: that if he was a כהן גדול and he was also a נזיר,
for his brother he does not become impure,
but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאָחִיו שֶׁאִם הָיָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְהוּא נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי עקיבא's reading with the next word in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a person who is both a כהן גדול and a נזיר may become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.title: For his sister: the case of someone going to bring his פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא uses 'לאחותו' for the same ברייתא quoted earlier, about someone on his way to bring his פסח or circumcise his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For his sister' is learned as it was taught in a ברייתא: someone who was going to slaughter his פסח or to circumcise his son, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא finishes his reading. He uses 'לאחותו' the same way the earlier ברייתא did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי עקיבא agrees with the earlier reading. 'לאחותו' teaches that a person on the way to an important מצוה may not become impure for his sister, but must become impure for a מת מצוה. Notice that the word 'ולאמו' has now been used up, with nothing left over for רבי's גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: For his sister
His קרבן פסח
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: "For his sister" — as it was taught in a ברייתא:
Here is one who was going
to slaughter his פסח offering
or to circumcise his son, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." means finish the ברייתא we already saw in steps 8 and 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי עקיבא's reading by explaining the last word, 'לאחותו'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לאחותו' teaches the case of someone going to bring his פסח or circumcise his son, as in the earlier ברייתא.

steps.title: Where does רבי עקיבא get רבי's גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי עקיבא used up 'ולאמו', the גמרא asks how he learns the rule that רבי got from his גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי עקיבא, where does he learn the rule of רבי's גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רבי עקיבא's reading. The next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, the word 'ולאמו' was left free for רבי's גזירה שוה, which teaches that a כהן גדול is barred only from corpse impurity, not from other kinds of impurity. רבי עקיבא used 'ולאמו' together with 'לאביו' to teach the מת מצוה rule. So he has no extra word for רבי's lesson, and we need to know how he gets it.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places in the תורה
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva,
the גזירה שוה of רבי — from where does he get it?
phrases.notes: This is the גזירה שוה from step 6, the one that used the word 'ולאמו'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה דְּרַבִּי מְנָלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that רבי עקיבא's reading leaves no free word for רבי's גזירה שוה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי עקיבא learn the כהן גדול rule that רבי derived from 'ולאמו', now that this word is used up?

steps.title: A plain כהן גדול is treated like a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא needs no גזירה שוה. Since 'לאחיו' shows that the נזיר section already speaks about a כהן גדול, its rules apply to a plain כהן גדול too, including the rule that only corpse impurity is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: the Master already said that a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר may not become impure for his brother, but may become impure for a מת מצוה. What difference does it make whether he is only a כהן גדול or both a נזיר and a כהן גדול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי עקיבא. He gets the rule from 'לאחיו' (step 11), so he does not need the גזירה שוה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's גזירה שוה taught that a כהן גדול, like a נזיר, is barred only from corpse impurity. For רבי עקיבא, 'לאחיו' shows that the נזיר section itself already deals with a כהן גדול. So there is no difference between a plain כהן גדול and one who is also a נזיר, and the נזיר section's rule (only corpse impurity is forbidden) covers a כהן גדול without a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to me? (there is no difference)
Alone, by himself
He would say to you

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, 'לאחיו' links the כהן גדול to the נזיר section. So the rule from רבי's גזירה שוה, that a כהן גדול is barred only from corpse impurity, follows without a separate word.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
Since the Master said
phrases.notes: "The Master" is רבי עקיבא's own teaching on 'לאחיו' from step 11.

phrases.english: if he was a כהן גדול and a נזיר,
for his brother he does not become impure,
but he does become impure for a מת מצוה —
what difference is it to me if he is only a כהן גדול,
or if he is both a נזיר and a כהן גדול?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 by drawing the rule out of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לאחיו' shows the נזיר section covers a כהן גדול. Since a plain כהן גדול is no different from one who is also a נזיר, the נזיר's rule that only corpse impurity is forbidden applies to him, so no גזירה שוה is needed.

steps.title: How does רבי ישמעאל know the rule for a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי ישמעאל learns that a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר may become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי ישמעאל, from where does he learn the rule for a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches from רבי עקיבא to רבי ישמעאל. It asks where he gets the rule that רבי עקיבא learned from 'לאחיו'. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רבי עקיבא used 'לאחיו' to teach that a person who is both a כהן גדול and a נזיר may bury a מת מצוה. רבי ישמעאל follows the first reading (steps 1-9), where 'לאחיו' was already used for the basic מת מצוה allowance (step 6). So that word is not free for this case, and the גמרא wants to know how he reaches the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose reading of the פסוקים differs from רבי עקיבא's
From where does he know it?
A person who is both a כהן גדול and a נזיר, so two separate prohibitions apply to him

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yishmael,
a High Priest who is also a nazirite, from where does he know it?
phrases.notes: This is the same case רבי עקיבא learned from 'לאחיו' back in step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְהוּא נָזִיר מְנָלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches from רבי עקיבא's readings (steps 10-14) to ask about רבי ישמעאל's source for the rule in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי ישמעאל's source for permitting a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר to become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.title: One prohibition or two makes no difference
steps.stepSummary: Once the Torah allows breaking one לאו for a מת מצוה, it allows breaking two as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah allowed one לאו to be set aside for a מת מצוה, what difference does it make to me whether it is one לאו or two לאוין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל needs no פסוק for this. Simple logic is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already allows a כהן גדול alone, or a נזיר alone, to become impure for a מת מצוה. A person who is both faces two לאוין instead of one. The permission for a מת מצוה is not limited by how many prohibitions are involved, so both are set aside.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (literally, 'the Merciful One') permitted
A negative commandment, a 'do not'

keyTerms.term: מָה לִי חַד, מָה לִי תְּרֵין
keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between one and two?

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי ישמעאל, the double case of כהן גדול plus נזיר needs no פסוק. If one לאו gives way for a מת מצוה, two give way too.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One permitted
one prohibition regarding a met מצוה,
phrases.notes: The one prohibition is either the כהן גדול's or the נזיר's.

phrases.english: what difference is it to me if it is one prohibition,
or two prohibitions?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּשְׁרָא רַחֲמָנָא חַד לָאו גַּבֵּי מֵת מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 with logic instead of a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No פסוק is needed. Permission to set aside one לאו for a מת מצוה covers two לאוין as well.

steps.title: Why does the Torah need the word 'his sister'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why 'אחותו' is needed to teach that one may become impure for a מת מצוה even on the way to his פסח or his son's מילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a separate word is needed for the case of someone going to bring his פסח or circumcise his son. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that a מת מצוה pushes aside the לאוין of a נזיר and a כהן. So it seems obvious that it should also push aside פסח and מילה. The גמרא asks why the Torah spends a word on it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'His sister', a word in the נזיר פסוק (במדבר 6:7)
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: Why do I need 'his sister'?
phrases.notes: In step 12 this word taught the case of someone on his way to bring his פסח or circumcise his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that the number of לאוין makes no difference, the גמרא asks why the פסח and מילה case needs its own word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a separate word is needed for the פסח and מילה case, if a מת מצוה already overrides other prohibitions.

steps.title: Even a מצוה with כרת gives way to a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Without 'אחותו' we might have thought that a מת מצוה only overrides לאוין, not מצוות like פסח and מילה that carry כרת. The word teaches that it overrides them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that the Torah allowed becoming impure for a מת מצוה only for a נזיר and a כהן, whose prohibitions are just לאוין. But for מילה and פסח, which carry כרת, perhaps one may not become impure for a מת מצוה. So the פסוק teaches us that he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'אחותו' is needed. Without it, we might have thought that a מצוה with the heavier punishment of כרת is too important to give way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibitions of a נזיר and a כהן are plain לאוין. Not bringing a פסח or not doing מילה carries כרת, which is far more severe. So the earlier rules alone would not prove that a מת מצוה beats them. 'אחותו' teaches that even these give way to burying a מת מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken first thought)
Being 'cut off', a severe punishment from Heaven
A prohibition that is only a לאו, lighter than כרת
It teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: Burying a מת מצוה is so important that it overrides even מצוות that carry כרת, like פסח and מילה. That is what 'אחותו' teaches.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'אחותו' is extra because we already know a מת מצוה overrides לאוין. כרת is a heavier category, so the earlier rules could not prove this case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how high a מת מצוה ranks: it outweighs even מצוות punished with כרת.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say
that when the Merciful One permitted becoming impure for a met מצוה,
that was for a nazirite and a priest,
since theirs is only a prohibition of negative commandments.
But circumcision and the Paschal offering, which carry karet,
perhaps one should not become impure for a met מצוה;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא כִּי שְׁרָא רַחֲמָנָא לְמֵת מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by showing why 'אחותו' teaches something new.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אחותו' teaches that a מת מצוה overrides even מצוות punishable by כרת (פסח and מילה), not only plain לאוין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מת מצוה overrides only plain לאוין, like those of a נזיר and a כהן, but not מצוות that carry כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even פסח and מילה, which carry כרת, give way to burying a מת מצוה.
